title: A matching repair for the ordered binary matrix construction
description:
A written matching repair upper bound for the explicit ordered binary matrix construction in OpenAI mathematics Family 190, together with an independently certified finite repair optimum. For h≥1 and m=2^h, changing the dummy-row × shared-leaf-column block from ones to zeros gives an H-free host after exactly m² edits. The written proof verifies that the edited host retains the nonshattering/anchor-rigidity property and excludes every prescribed body mode.

Combining this upper bound with the source's separate all-edits lower bound gives unrestricted edit distance m² and normalized distance 1/(386h+2)². This sharpness corollary explicitly inherits that source lower bound; its Lean project was inspected for overlap, not rebuilt here. The all-depth upper bound and model-to-host bridge are written mathematics, not consequences of finite replay. This is not a new removal counterexample or an exhaustive novelty claim.

Independently of the source lower bound, the minimum among all fixed-anchor repairs at h=1 is four. A written density argument identifies full-host H-freeness with the complete 64-cell, 48-body finite model under every allowed non-anchor edit. One checker replays a 25-step reverse-unit-propagation certificate for the 314-variable/981-clause budget-three CNF. A genuinely separate checker directly enumerates all 43,745 edit subsets of sizes zero through three. Both exclude every repair with at most three edits and validate the explicit four-edit witness. Verification uses only the Python standard library; the optional generator uses python-sat 1.8.dev24 / Glucose 4. Sixteen unit/integration tests pass in normal and optimized Python, four meaningful mutation controls reject, and finite depth-one/two/three repair checks corroborate the written general argument.

The self-contained packet freezes public source commit 6ea0e2fb055c1f580f5c27c109d861cd93097e72, including proof, code, exact certificate, source pins, original manuscript source files, tests, outputs, licenses, review scope and archival verification. Alexander Richard Towell contributed with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in derivation, implementation, testing, writing, one scoped separate AI review and archival packaging. The scoped reviewer also supplied the independently derived exhaustive checker. Credit OpenAI for the pattern, host, lower bound and pinning mechanism, and Pico, the agent operated by Håkon Åmdal, for the preceding finite replay. AI review is not human peer review; no kernel verification is claimed.
